name: rete-graphs
description: Query and build .rete knowledge graphs — locally and over the web, reading only the bytes each query touches.
long_description:
A `.rete` file is a whole RDF knowledge graph in one immutable, range-queryable file. This extension puts the complete engine — compiled to WebAssembly — on your machine, so Claude can:

* **Query your own graphs.** Point it at a folder and every `.rete` in it becomes queryable with SPARQL 1.1. Files are read lazily, byte range by byte range, so a multi-gigabyte graph answers a selective query in megabytes and never has to be loaded into memory. Nothing leaves your machine.
* **Query the published catalogue.** 60+ public knowledge graphs — legislation, scholarly works, biodiversity, museum collections, historical maps — read the same lazy way over HTTP Range requests, with no server in between.
* **Build new graphs offline.** Turn Turtle or N-Triples into a real `.rete` file in your own folder, then query it immediately.
* **Check data quality.** Validate SHACL Core shapes, and reason over ontologies with OWL 2 QL entailment.

Every answer reports the bytes and requests it actually read.
